description: Volatility-Indexed Contextual Thompson Restart (VICTR): Step 1: Maintain a sliding window of the last 512 learned clause LBDs and calculate the Coefficient of Variation (CV = standard deviation / mean). Step 2: Discretize the search state into three contexts based on CV: 'Stagnant' (CV < 0.6), 'Steady' (0.6 <= CV <= 1.4), and 'Volatile' (CV > 1.4). Step 3: For each context, maintain a Thompson Sampling model with three arms: Arm 0 (Luby-style restarts), Arm 1 (Aggressive EMA-based restarts), and Arm 2 (Lazy EMA-based restarts). Step 4: When 'restart_mab' is invoked, identify the current context and sample a value from the Beta distribution (alpha, beta) of each arm within that context, selecting the arm with the highest sample. Step 5: Define the reward R as (Global_Average_LBD / Window_Average_LBD) * (Current_Conflicts_Per_Second / Global_Average_CPS). Step 6: Update the chosen arm's parameters: if R > 1.0, increment alpha by R; otherwise, increment beta by (1/R). Step 7: Apply a decay factor of 0.95 to all alpha/beta values every 10,000 conflicts to ensure the bandit remains responsive to the shifting landscape of the SAT formula.
analysis: Standard MABs in solvers ignore the search context; VICTR uses LBD volatility to detect if the solver is stuck in a local plateau or traversing a complex landscape, selecting restart frequency accordingly.
